Our client, Tech Envision, is a technology solutions provider located in Warrnambool, Victoria, specialising in telecommunications, networking, information technology (IT) infrastructure, and digital technology services. The company delivers end-to-end solutions including network design, telecommunications system deployment, infrastructure implementation, technical support, and ongoing maintenance for business clients. 

Tech Envision is seeking a Telecommunications Field Engineer to install, commission, maintain, troubleshoot, and support telecommunications and network infrastructure at customer sites. The role involves delivering field engineering services, ensuring reliable network performance, resolving technical issues, and providing high-quality customer support while complying with industry standards and safety requirements.

The annual salary for this position is $75,000 to $85,000.

Duties include:

•	Conduct site surveys to assess customer requirements, network infrastructure, equipment locations, and installation feasibility for telecommunications projects. 

•	Install, configure, commission, and test telecommunications equipment, including routers, switches, wireless devices, fibre optic systems, Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) solutions, and network hardware to meet technical specifications. 

•	Perform fault diagnosis, preventive maintenance, and corrective repairs on telecommunications networks and associated equipment to ensure continuous service availability. 

•	Monitor network performance using diagnostic tools and protocol analysers, identifying faults and implementing technical solutions to optimise system reliability and efficiency. 

•	Configure Internet Protocol (IP) networking, routing, switching, Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs), Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), and wireless communication systems in accordance with customer requirements and industry standards. 

•	Conduct fibre optic cable testing, splicing verification, signal measurements, and certification using specialised test equipment to ensure network integrity and performance. 

•	Prepare technical documentation, including installation reports, network diagrams, test results, maintenance records, and equipment configuration details for project completion and compliance purposes. 

•	Provide onsite technical support and troubleshooting for customers, resolving hardware, software, connectivity, and telecommunications service issues within agreed service levels. 

•	Coordinate with Project Managers, Network Engineers, vendors, and customers during installation, commissioning, upgrades, and maintenance activities to ensure successful project delivery. 

•	Ensure all telecommunications installations and field activities comply with workplace health and safety requirements, telecommunications regulations, and company quality standards. 

•	Perform system upgrades, firmware updates, equipment replacements, and network expansion activities with minimal disruption to customer operations. 

•	Assist in evaluating new telecommunications technologies, conducting field testing and performance validation, and recommending improvements to enhance network capability, reliability, and customer service outcomes.

Qualifications:

•	Must have at least one (1) year of experience.

•	Should hold a Diploma or higher qualification in a relevant field.

Measure, mark out, and prepare installation reference points for electrical systems and equipment.
Select, cut, terminate, and connect electrical wiring and cables to switches, outlets, control devices, and other electrical components.

Repair and replace faulty wiring, electrical components, and other defective parts.
Install, connect, and commission electrical switchboards, distribution boards, and associated equipment.
Connect electrical systems and equipment to power supplies in accordance with applicable standards and regulations.

Current electrical licence or registration as required in Western Australia.
Sound knowledge of electrical systems, wiring methods, and Australian Standards.
Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings and technical documentation.

Strong fault-finding and problem-solving skills.

result.description:
Colormaker Industries Australia is a well-established, family-owned manufacturer of quality coatings for interior and exterior application. Amongst a broad range of technologies, Colormaker also manufactures and exports market leading world class products in textile screen printing inks and high solids epoxy swimming pool coatings. The business is based on Sydney’s Northern Beaches.

We require a dedicated coatings & inks Quality Control (QC) Chemist to join our busy team of specialists in Brookvale, NSW.

Reporting to the Senior Chemist and Technical Manager, the duties and responsibilities of the role will include:

. Performing laboratory tests/QC procedures on paints and raw materials and recommending improvements for Factory Production and Product Development
. Preparing materials for test and/or experimentation
. Performing calculations, computations and measurements
. Analyzing test data results and preparing relevant reviews, reports and summaries
. Auditing and controlling the quality and quantity of materials used in QC tests, R&D and product maintenance
. Checking, calibrating and maintaining test equipment and other laboratory facilities
. Management of Safety Data Sheets, both Raw Materials and Finished Goods
. Technical and other support to Customer Service and Marketing, including translation of technical and other product literature
. Proficient use of Tencia/Arrow, Color I Control and relevant business software (including MS EXCEL). Also use of company systems
. Maintenance of relevant QC and Production records and related administration
. Adhering to appropriate workplace health and safety standards and making recommendations for improvement
. Management of Hazardous Materials and Dangerous Goods.
. Advising and sourcing materials for Research and Development (R&D) projects
. Carrying out product development work on new and existing products

We offer a competitive remuneration package of between $70,000 to $85,000 per annum, excluding superannuation.

The successful candidate will have either:

. A relevant AQF Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma or Diploma plus five (5) years’ work experience; or
. At least ten (10) years of relevant full-time work experience

The successful candidate must have coatings experience. In particular, high solids epoxy, high performance industrial surface coatings, broad wall architectural and construction membranes etc would be highly regarded, as would knowledge of textile and other screen printing ink technologies. They must also be passionate about the environment, have a good eye for colour and for detail as well as an ability to work with minimal supervision. A high degree of numeracy and literacy in English are mandatory, whilst technical fluency in European languages would be highly regarded.  Applicants must have full and permanent working rights in Australia to be considered.

If you feel that you are suited to the role of Quality Control Chemist, then please send your CV to us via email technical@colormaker.com.au.

- Seeking an Organisation and Methods (Quality Classing) Analyst
- Salary $80,000 + superannuation
- Join Australian Food and Fibre

Australian Food & Fibre (AFF) is a modern, integrated business that combines significant knowledge and expertise to supply quality Australian cotton to the world, as well as cereals, pulses and oil seeds.

We have a career opportunity for a skilled Organisation & Methods (Quality Classing) Analyst to join our team in our Artarmon laboratory, 2064, New South Wales.

Overall Responsibilities:

At the Australian Food & Fibre, Artarmon, facility you are responsible for testing, evaluating and grading our agricultural commodities. They ensure that raw materials (primarily cotton) meet strict domestic and international quality standards before they are exported or sold.

Daily tasks:
- Fibre testing - operating specialised laboratory instruments to analyse the physical properties of cotton samples. This includes measuring fibre length, strength, micronaire (fineness), maturity, and colour.
- Assess current systems - analyse and evaluate capabilities, and workflows to identify bottlenecks and process gaps.
- Commodity grading - applying standardised classing rules to assign grades to cotton lint. This determines the market value and spinning utility of the crop.
- Sample management - preparing, tracking, and cataloguing physical samples sent from various AFF farming and ginning operations (such as their sites in Moree and Narrabri).
- Data Analysis - recording and verifying data within classing and laboratory software systems, ensuring that every batch meets the requirements of export contracts.
- Quality assurance - monitoring laboratory equipment calibration to ensure accurate and reliable test results.
- Classing and compliance - develop, maintain and enforce Quality Auditor standards, reviewing operating procedures and advising on any departures from established guidelines.

Our ideal candidate will have:
- Hands-on trade experience through on-the-job training OR Certificate III in Cotton Ginning OR specialised industry-recognised classing grader advantageous OR an IT background will better equip you with the analytical skills required in our laboratory and for this role.
- Minimum 2+ years of experience in procedural/business/computer analysis, continuous improvement or quality control
- A Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business, IT, Commerce, Operations Management or a related field will be highly regarded.

While a formal agricultural degree can be advantageous for career advancement with us, our hands-on approach for you to function well in the role is to assist you in gaining certification from Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry as part of your induction with us and a requirement for our quality control and cotton exporting criteria.

In return, we can offer:
- Highly competitive salary package ($80,000 + super)
- Excellent professional development and career progression opportunities.
- Supportive, dynamic team environment with hybrid working arrangements.
- Opportunities for ongoing employment and training across seasonal operations.
- Contribution to the local agricultural economy in our regional NSW operations.

Join our company and enjoy a supportive, family-friendly environment where you'll receive in-house assistance and continuous opportunities for up-skilling, ensuring your ongoing professional growth.
